explain.say: Every part of a structure is being pulled or pushed. A pull that stretches is called tension, and a push that squashes is called compression.

Tension is the force in a rope holding a swing, or in the cables of a suspension bridge. Even a thin steel cable can carry huge loads in tension, because there is nothing to bend or buckle.

faq.a: Tension is a pulling force that stretches a part. Ropes, cables and chains work in tension, and steel is very strong this way.
asks: What does tension mean in engineering?

faq.a: Compression is a pushing force that squashes a part. Columns, walls and arches work in compression, and stone, brick and concrete are strong this way.
Buckling is when a long, thin part in compression suddenly bows out sideways and fails, long before the material itself is crushed. That is why columns are made thick or braced.
asks: Why does a straw fold when you push its ends?

faq.q: Why is concrete weak in tension?
faq.a: Concrete is stones glued by cement, and when it is pulled, tiny cracks open and spread easily. Its tensile strength is only about a tenth of its compressive strength, so steel bars are added where it will be stretched.
asks: Why does concrete crack when pulled?

faq.q: Which parts of a bridge are in tension and which in compression?
faq.a: In a suspension bridge the cables are in tension and the towers in compression. In an arch bridge the arch is in compression, and in a beam the top is squashed while the bottom is stretched.
asks: Where is tension in a bridge?

facts: Concrete's tensile strength is roughly one tenth of its compressive strength.
A beam carrying a load is in compression along its top face and in tension along its bottom face.

quiz.say: The main cables of a suspension bridge are mostly under which kind of force?
quiz.why: The cables are pulled tight by the weight of the deck hanging from them, so they are stretched, which is tension.

wrong.1: Compression is squashing, which towers and arches carry; a squashed cable would just go slack.
wrong.2: The cables carry the whole deck, so they are under very large force.
